blocks.orig: Climbing Kilimanjaro via the steep 6-day Umbwe Route
blocks.html: Climb Kilimanjaro on the steep 6-day Umbwe Route

blocks.orig: Umbwe route is the shortest of all routes in terms of the distance you travel to the top of Kilimanjaro. Therefore, the increase in altitude per day is very high. You hike steep through the valley and directly up to the summit. Because this route is so extreme and demands a lot from your body, it is also known as the “Double Whiskey Route”. The Umbwe route is only suitable for climbers who have already been at a comparable altitude and know how their body reacts to such an extreme increase in altitude.
blocks.html: Measured by the distance you cover to the summit of Kilimanjaro, the Umbwe route is the shortest one. As a result, you gain a great deal of altitude each day. The trail climbs steeply through the valley and heads straight for the summit. Because it is so extreme and asks so much of your body, people also call it the “Double Whiskey Route”. The Umbwe route only suits climbers who have been at a similar altitude before and know how their body copes with such a sharp rise in altitude.

blocks.orig: If you want to add another day to the Umbwe route, this is of course possible and even recommended. An extra day gives your body more time to get used to the altitude and increases the chance that you will reach the top of Kilimanjaro without suffering from altitude sickness.
blocks.html: Adding an extra day to the Umbwe route is of course possible, and we even advise it. With one more day your body has more time to adapt to the altitude, which improves your chances of reaching the top of Kilimanjaro without altitude sickness.

blocks.orig: Your Tanzania Trip offers a unique service throughout the climb
blocks.html: Your Tanzania Trip gives you a special service for the whole climb

blocks.orig: Climbing Kilimanjaro is the ultimate challenge! Little details can make a world of difference, which is why with us, you climb with professional guides, porters, and a cook. They take care of you during your ascent via the Umbwe route, by checking your health twice a day and serving you delicious food. Sounds like a bit much? Not if you want to reach the top! Because we know that altitude sickness can creep up on you unnoticed and that proper nutrition* is essential to keep you going during a strenuous climb.
blocks.html: Climbing Kilimanjaro is a challenge like no other! The small things can make all the difference, which is why you climb with us alongside professional guides, porters and a cook. While you ascend the Umbwe route, they look after you, checking your health twice a day and preparing tasty meals. Does that sound like too much? Not if you are aiming for the summit! We know that altitude sickness can sneak up on you without warning, and that good nutrition* is vital to keep you going on a tough climb.

blocks.orig: *If you would like to see the menu, we can send it in advance.
blocks.html: *Would you like to see the menu? We are happy to send it beforehand.

blocks.orig: If you like advice on how to prepare yourself for climbing Kilimanjaro, you can always contact us or read our blog How to prepare for climbing Kilimanjaro?
blocks.html: Would you like tips on getting ready to climb Kilimanjaro? Just get in touch with us, or read our blog How do you prepare for climbing Kilimanjaro?

blocks.orig: When you arrive at Kilimanjaro International Airport our Your Tanzania Trip guide is there waiting for you. He then drops you off at your hotel, where you can relax from your flight.
blocks.html: On arrival at Kilimanjaro International Airport you are met by our Your Tanzania Trip guide. He takes you to your hotel, where you can unwind after the flight.

blocks.orig: Preparation for your climb: You meet your guide before the start of your climb, where he briefs you and offers advice on what to wear, what to pack, and other important tips to make your climb as comfortable as possible.
blocks.html: Getting ready for your climb: Ahead of the climb you meet your guide, who briefs you and gives advice on clothing, packing and other key tips so your climb is as comfortable as it can be.

blocks.orig: Today, your driver picks you up at the hotel and takes you to the Umbwe Gate to complete the registration formalities. The Kilimanjaro climb begins through dense rainforest, where you can hear and spot various animals. As you approach the Umbwe River, the route becomes steeper, offering views of Kibo Peak in the distance and the deep valleys surrounding you. The climb ends after 5-7 hours at Umbwe Cave Camp.
blocks.html: Today your driver collects you at the hotel and brings you to the Umbwe Gate, where you complete the registration formalities. Your Kilimanjaro climb starts in thick rainforest, where you can hear and see all kinds of animals. Nearer the Umbwe River the trail gets steeper, with views of Kibo Peak far ahead and of the deep valleys around you. After 5-7 hours the day's climb finishes at Umbwe Cave Camp.

blocks.orig: Leave the rainforest and enter the heather with rocks and valleys around you. The ascent becomes steeper at the Umbwe Route Ridge and flattens out again near the Barranco Valley. After a 4 to 5-hour hike, you have dinner and overnight at the Barranco Camp in the valley below the Barranco wall.
blocks.html: You leave the rainforest behind and move into heather, with rocks and valleys all around. At the Umbwe Route Ridge the climb gets steeper, then levels off again close to the Barranco Valley. After hiking for 4 to 5 hours, you have dinner and spend the night at Barranco Camp, in the valley beneath the Barranco wall.

blocks.orig: This morning, you hike to the Barranco Wall where you have a spectacular view of the Kibo volcano to the left and Mount Meru to the right. Then a more difficult route to Karanga Camp begins, with many ascents and descents. Once at the camp, you have lunch and a couple of hours to rest. You can then go on a 300-meter acclimatization hike towards Barafu Camp before descending back to Karanga Camp for the night.
blocks.html: This morning's hike brings you to the Barranco Wall, with a spectacular view of Mount Meru on your right and the Kibo volcano on your left. Next comes a tougher stretch to Karanga Camp, with plenty of climbs and descents. At the camp you have lunch and a few hours of rest. Then you can do a 300-meter acclimatization hike towards Barafu Camp, before heading back down to Karanga Camp to sleep.

blocks.orig: On the fourth day on the mountain, you walk to Barafu Camp, the starting point for your summit push to Uhuru Peak. Arrive at the camp around noon, enjoy lunch, and take some time to rest. Later, go on another acclimatization walk to Kosovo Summit Camp (4,870 m) before returning to Barafu Camp. Warm up with a hot dinner and relax for the rest of the day before starting the climb to the top of Kili at midnight.
blocks.html: On your fourth day on the mountain you hike to Barafu Camp, from where you start your summit push to Uhuru Peak. You reach the camp at about midday, have lunch and rest for a while. Later on you do one more acclimatization walk to Kosovo Summit Camp (4,870 m) and then return to Barafu Camp. A hot dinner warms you up, and you spend the rest of the day relaxing before you set off for the top of Kili at midnight.

blocks.orig: Around midnight, you begin your final push to Uhuru Peak. Ascend along good trails while your guide keeps an eye on you to monitor your physical and mental state facing the altitude. Once you reach the top, enjoy a beautiful sunrise from the roof of Africa! After celebrating at the top, descend to the nearby glacier before returning through Barafu Camp and continuing the descent to Millennium Camp after a two-hour break.
blocks.html: At about midnight your final push to Uhuru Peak begins. You climb on good trails while your guide watches how you are coping, physically and mentally, with the altitude. At the top, take in a beautiful sunrise from the roof of Africa! Once you have celebrated on the summit, you go down to the nearby glacier, then back via Barafu Camp, where you take a two-hour break before continuing down to Millennium Camp.

blocks.orig: Millenium Camp is located in a tropical rainforest. Here you feel a sense of relief from the reduced altitude and satisfaction from reaching the summit the day before. After breakfast, you walk to the national park's exit and your driver takes you back to the hotel, where you can recover from the rigors of the climb.
blocks.html: Millenium Camp lies in tropical rainforest. Here you feel relieved to be at a lower altitude and satisfied at having reached the summit the day before. After breakfast you walk to the exit of the national park, and your driver brings you back to the hotel so you can recover from the demands of the climb.

blocks.orig: Sadly, this is the end of your holiday and the time to go home has arrived. Enjoy your last hours in Tanzania before our driver comes to pick you up and takes you to Kilimanjaro International Airport for your flight home. Still longing for more? It's also possible to add a few days of safari or a beach holiday to your Kilimanjaro adventure!
blocks.html: Unfortunately your holiday has come to a close and it is time to head home. Make the most of your last hours in Tanzania until our driver collects you and takes you to Kilimanjaro International Airport for your flight. Not ready to say goodbye? You can also extend your Kilimanjaro adventure with a few days of safari or a beach holiday!
